messages:
elaine: quick sweep results from this morning — brought up gpt-adv-7b quant-8 across US-E / US-W / EU-W on H100 vs A100. wanted to share p50/p95 and a few hypotheses.

elaine: test setup: 512 seq, minibatch=1 steady-state, 2000 warmup tokens, kernel: flash-attn vs fallback-causal, edge routing: direct-pop vs edge-proxy.

elaine: raw numbers (ms):
H100 direct-pop: us-east p50=18 p95=42 | us-west p50=20 p95=44 | eu-west p50=26 p95=65
H100 via edge-proxy: us-east p50=20 p95=55 | us-west p50=23 p95=61 | eu-west p50=33 p95=95
A100 direct-pop: us-east p50=28 p95=70 | us-west p50=30 p95=78 | eu-west p50=38 p95=110
A100 via edge-proxy: us-east p50=32 p95=95 | us-west p50=34 p95=102 | eu-west p50=44 p95=150

elaine: observations:
- H100 consistently lower p50/p95 than A100 for same config (expected).
- edge-proxy adds modest p50 but large p95 tail in eu-west (not linear).
- flash-attn kernel wins ~10-15% p50 vs fallback but can worsen p95 when combined with proxy in eu-west.

raj: nice. do you have per-hop counts or e2e traceroutes?

elaine: yes — attached the traceroute summary (pasted):
us-east direct route hops=6 avg-rtt=12ms
us-west direct route hops=7 avg-rtt=15ms
eu-west direct route hops=12 avg-rtt=22ms
eu-west via-proxy hops=18 avg-rtt=40ms

noah: so proxy increases hop count and RTT variance -> explains p95 explosion in eu-west. likely cross-POP egress queuing.

claire: is this with continuous batching turned on? batching changes kernel selection heuristics right?

elaine: batching disabled for these microbenchmarks (minibatch=1) to measure single-request latency. did run a few with batch=4: p50 improves ~8-12% but p95 marginally better only on H100 direct.

raj: kernel detail? flash-attn config vs fallback: did you pin cuBLAS or Triton kernels?

elaine: flash-attn (optimized fused kernels) on H100 via Triton; fallback is our generic causal matmul path using cuBLAS. On A100, flash-attn still helps but memory layout + quantized kernels add overhead that bumps tail when network variance high.

noah: for capacity planning: what's tokens/sec throughput at target tail?

elaine: rough steady throughput (tokens/s) for seq512, batch1: H100 direct ~950 tok/s, A100 direct ~620 tok/s. If we size for 99th percentile <100ms in us-east, need ~1.5x capacity for A100 vs H100.

claire: recommendation for routing and kernel defaults?

elaine: provisional:
- default: H100s keep flash-attn on for direct-pop.
- for edge-proxy routes, prefer fallback kernel on eu-west for quant-8 on A100 to curb p95 spikes (empirically more stable).
- add routing policy: prefer regional direct-pop when p95 > 2x baseline for 5m.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary routing change to prefer direct-pop in eu-west at 2026-03-20T14:00Z if ops approves.

raj: can we add a quick canary that flips kernel heuristic to prefer fallback when edge-proxy present? avoid full rollback.

elaine: yes, I can push a config canary. will run 1% traffic for 30m then measure p95.

noah: also add a small synthetic probe that emits 10 calls every 30s to track p95 drift per-pop. put metric under /redwood/inference/edge/p95-probe.

claire: sounding good. if probe shows >20% p95 increase over 10m, auto-route to backup pop.

elaine: will open a quick PR for the canary and probe dashboards. tl;dr: H100+direct best, proxy increases tail especially in eu-west, fallback kernel stabilizes tail on A100 quant builds.

raj: thanks — this helps sizing and default routing policy.

noah: nice work, please paste PR and results once canary runs. :thumbsup:
